reason: The injury must occur before the body can respond to bleeding, and the rough edge is the visible cause.
expectation: The rough edge should create a small skin and vessel injury.

effect: The cut and narrowed bleeding vessel are now present, so the clotting response can begin.
reaction: The vessel narrowing is a useful detail.
reason: Platelets can gather at the damaged vessel to help stop the bleeding.
expectation: Platelets will form an initial plug at the injury.

effect: The platelet plug slows the leak; clotting factors and fibrinogen may reinforce it.
reaction: The initial plug makes the next clotting step clear.
reason: Activated clotting factors should convert soluble fibrinogen into fibrin that strengthens the plug.
expectation: Fibrin will form for a stabilizing clot.

alternatives.reason: The factors might instead act directly at the plug.

effect: The clotting factors produced fibrin threads, which can now reinforce the platelet plug.
reaction: The thread mesh makes the reinforcement step clear.
reason: Fibrin threads should stabilize the plug at the damaged vessel.
expectation: A fibrin-reinforced clot will stop the bleeding.

effect: The fibrin mesh stabilized the platelet plug and stopped the bleeding, while the skin remained open.
reaction: The distinction between sealing the vessel and closing the skin was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Reinforcing the platelet plug with fibrin was the most worthwhile construction: it showed how the initial plug becomes stable without implying the whole wound has healed.

leastWorthwhile.text: Creating the cut was predictable setup rather than a meaningful decision, though it established the injury clearly.

surprise.text: The result showed the vessel narrowing immediately after the cut, before platelets formed a plug.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although combining fibrinogen with already activated factors leaves their activation unexplained.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the still-open skin repairs itself after the bleeding stops.
